answer: The zenith multiplier is published, charged in vine, and meadow lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4276 identities would post 4667 proofs and burn roughly 72 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
